{'index': 0, 'translation': 'The Labour Department announced today (the 10th) that Hua Sao Ice Room (Prince Edward) is suspected of providing false information when applying for imported labour, and has been subject to administrative sanctions by the department. The Supplementary Labour Optimization Scheme has been in place for three years since its launch in September 2023. The Labour Department replied that as of July this year, it had received a total of 1,365 complaints, of which 111 warning letters were issued to employers suspected of violations, and another 17 cases suspected of violating imported labour regulations and 31 cases suspected of violating other laws resulted in convictions and administrative sanctions. Together with the Hua Sao Ice Room (Prince Edward) whose sanctions were just announced today, The Collective has compiled 18 companies penalised for violating imported labour regulations, of which 10 are in the catering services and cleaning industries. Why were they penalised? Of the 18 companies, 9 are suspected of unreasonably refusing to hire local job seekers, and most of them have been refused imported labour applications for the following two years by the Labour Department; another two restaurants dismissed local employees after importing foreign workers, and their already-approved foreign worker quotas were immediately revoked.'}

{'index': 1, 'translation': 'As of today, the Labour Department has imposed administrative sanctions on a total of 18 employers who violated the Supplementary Labour Optimization Scheme, all of whom have had their applications suspended for one to two years.'}

{'index': 2, 'translation': "The Supplementary Labour Optimization Scheme has been in place since September 2023, but amid a sluggish market and rising unemployment and underemployment rates, the government's continued importation of foreign labour has raised concerns. In August 2025, the authorities announced the first administrative sanction case, involving a company refusing local job seekers without reasonable grounds, immediately suspending the company's application and rejecting foreign labour applications for the following year. In the same month, Secretary for Labour and Welfare Sun Yuk-han said the foreign labour mechanism does not tolerate abuse, and that in the future, depending on the severity of cases and public concern, the names of violating employers would be disclosed where feasible."}

{'index': 3, 'translation': 'The Collective has compiled administrative sanction cases previously made public by the Labour Department. Together with Hua Sao Ice Room (Prince Edward), which was administratively sanctioned today, the Labour Department has administratively sanctioned at least 18 employers who violated imported labour regulations, of which 6 companies are in the catering services industry and 4 are cleaning service companies. Nine companies were sanctioned for refusing to hire local job seekers without reasonable grounds, including Tao Duo Duo (Tsuen Wan) Limited, Asia Cleaning Services, and Sin Hang Professional Elderly Home, among others; the positions involved include general clerks, warehouse keepers, cleaners, air-conditioning technical assistants, and more. Of the 9 companies, 8 have had their foreign labour applications for the following two years rejected by the Labour Department.'}

{'index': 4, 'translation': 'In August last year, Sheung Yuen was administratively sanctioned by the Labour Department for dismissing local employees after hiring foreign workers. (File photo)'}

{'index': 5, 'translation': 'In addition, 5 companies are suspected of providing false information — submitting untrue applicant data, local employee numbers, and open recruitment results to the Labour Department — including Little Girl Money Exchange Limited, Tai Li Frozen Meat, and Hua Sao Ice Room (Prince Edward), among others, all of which have had their applications suspended for one year.'}

{'index': 6, 'translation': 'In two cases, Sheung Yuen Banquet Hall Limited, which operates Sheung Yuen Chinese Restaurant, and Able Showcase Group Limited, which operates Ying Yuen, were found to have dismissed local workers after hiring foreign workers. Their applications for the following two years were rejected, and their already-approved imported labour approvals were immediately revoked. However, the 11 foreign worker quotas already used by Sheung Yuen Chinese Restaurant can continue to remain in Hong Kong for work; Secretary for Labour and Welfare Sun Yuk-han said at the time that the relevant penalties were sufficiently deterrent to employers.'}

{'index': 7, 'translation': 'Three years into the implementation of the Supplementary Labour Optimization Scheme, the Labour Department has received a total of 1,365 complaints, of which approximately 8% of cases were issued warning letters, and approximately 3% were administratively sanctioned. (File photo)'}

{'index': 8, 'translation': 'Complaints last year increased tenfold year-on-year; 533 complaints received in the first 7 months of this year'}

{'index': 9, 'translation': "In reply to The Collective's enquiry today, the Labour Department said that as of July this year, the Supplementary Labour Optimization Scheme had received a total of 1,365 complaints — 14 in 2023, 69 in 2024, and a near tenfold year-on-year increase to 749 in 2025. As for the first 7 months of this year, 533 complaints have already been received. Of the 1,365 complaints, the Labour Department issued 111 warning letters to employers suspected of violations in cases where investigations had been completed, accounting for approximately 8% of complaints; there are 17 cases involving violations of the scheme's regulations that have been administratively sanctioned, with their imported labour applications suspended for one to two years. In addition, there are 31 cases where employers were convicted of illegal acts — for example, the Employees' Compensation Ordinance, occupational safety and health legislation, and the Immigration Ordinance — and were administratively sanctioned."}

{'index': 10, 'translation': 'In response to labour sector concerns about local worker unemployment, the authorities completed a review of the scheme in mid-June this year, introducing a two-tier approval system for the catering services industry, tightening the ratio of local full-time employees to foreign workers from 2:1 to 3:1, and extending the maximum administrative sanction period for violating employers to five years. In June and July, after the introduction of the two-tier system, the scheme received 94 and 85 complaints respectively, of which catering industry complaints remain the hardest-hit area, with 49 and 53 cases in the past two months, accounting for nearly 57%.'}
